wine-and-sommellerie.verdict: A craft where the qualification travels and the teacher does not, taught in three cities that live off the trade — and an exam you can genuinely fail

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Yes, in the institutional form, and this map already ruled on it: wine's teaching is institutional rather than a master you apprentice under. The bodies are named and so are their lineages — the Wine & Spirit Education Trust from Bermondsey, the Institute of Masters of Wine, the Court of Master Sommeliers, and the CIVB's own school in Bordeaux. No individual is named because the credential belongs to the body, not to the person who taught you for it, and that is the shape of this craft rather than thin research.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open on published dates from Level 1 upward, and the door has a lock on it. The WSET Diploma and the Master of Wine study programme are examined by the awarding body, blind, and people fail them repeatedly — the Master of Wine in particular is famous for it. That is the second half of this question answered better than almost anywhere here: your palate can fail in a way nobody can talk you past.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Yes. These are classroom cohorts working structured blind-tasting flights together, which is a craft you cannot practise alone — you calibrate against other people's palates or you calibrate against nothing. Napa carries the densest New World cohort of Diploma candidates, and London puts Level 1 students in the same building as the Diploma.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes, and Bordeaux settles it through the growers rather than the schools. The Union des Grands Crus de Bordeaux, founded in 1973, has 126 member châteaux across Médoc, Pessac-Léognan, Saint-Émilion, Pomerol and Sauternes, runs about 80 events a year worldwide, and put nearly 5,000 wine-trade professionals through the city over four days of En Primeur Week in April 2026. A city that fills for four days because of what is in the barrels is a place the trade belongs to.

evidence.what: the Union des Grands Crus de Bordeaux on its members and En Primeur Week

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. The ladder is the clearest on this map — WSET 1 to 4, then the Diploma, then the Master of Wine or the Master Sommelier — and it is public, examined and takes years by design. What it does not show is whether the room above the Diploma is open to you in these cities, which is a matter of who will pour for you, and nobody publishes that.

yacht-crew-and-stcw.verdict: Six towns that exist because of boats, teaching a legal minimum honestly — and not one instructor named, in a course whose whole value is the person running the fire ground

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Empty in all six places. Antibes, Palma, Cowes, Fort Lauderdale, Dover and Sydney list seven schools between them and not one named instructor. That is the shape of an MCA-approved course, where the syllabus and the approval belong to the flag state and the trainer is interchangeable by design. It is still worth asking: firefighting and sea survival are taught by people who did the job, or by people who did not, and the difference shows in four days.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open to anybody, which is the honest strength here. Four to five days, no sea experience assumed, MCA-approved, on published dates in six countries. And the hands can ruin it in the most literal way on this map: you enter a smoke house with a hose and you board a liferaft in a pool, and both are assessed because the failure mode at sea is death. This page is also honest about what the ticket is not — it gets you to an interview, and no school can promise a job.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Yes. Classroom and pool groups of roughly ten to twenty, in smaller teams on the fire ground and at the liferaft, and the people beside you are mostly going for their first boat — which in this trade is the cohort that becomes your network. Antibes is where that matters most: the schools, the agencies and the crew houses are inside the same square kilometre.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes, and both ends of this page settle it without a school's help. Port Vauban at Antibes calls itself the first yachting marina in the Mediterranean, with 1,500 berths and room for boats up to 150 metres, run under a 25-year public service delegation awarded by the City of Antibes. And Cowes sailed the bicentenary of Cowes Week in 2026 with 35 classes racing, already advertising 31 July to 6 August 2027. These are towns whose harbours and calendars are organised around boats, which is why the crew market is there at all.

evidence.what: Port Vauban's own site, on its berths and capacity
Cowes Week's own site, on the bicentenary regatta and the 2027 dates

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been on one of these courses. The ladder above STCW Basic is real and legible — sea time, then a departmental ticket, then the certificates of competency under the same convention — and this page already says so plainly. What no school can tell you is whether the town keeps you between boats, which in this trade is the whole question and is answered by a winter, not a brochure.

japanese-knife-making.verdict: A named smith who teaches it himself, in English, on a published date — and a forge in blade country that is not a knife town you can walk around

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Yes, and on the strictest reading of this question. Nobuya Hayashi is not a founder with his name over a door: he teaches the course himself, in English, without an interpreter, and he trained for years under Mitsunori Okada, a tamahagane specialist. The teacher and the man at the fire beside you are the same person, which is the thing this question is actually asking and the thing most forges on this craft cannot answer.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open, published and priced. A Wednesday-to-Sunday schedule running roughly September to May, bookable by anyone with no experience and no CV, at ¥44,000 for the one-day in 2026 and ¥48,000 for 2027 dates; the six-day tamahagane course runs ¥330,000–440,000 depending on the date. And your hands can ruin it — you forge, grind and quench the blade yourself, and a quench can go wrong in a way a smith can show you. Note what is honestly withheld rather than sold: the master keeps the most dangerous stages and puts the final whetstone edge on.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Nobody publishes the answer. The workshop advertises no class size, no group cap and no cohort, and we have not asked. A small countryside forge running a one-day course may well put you at the fire alone — which for this craft is arguably the better lesson and still not what this question asks. Until somebody publishes a number or somebody of ours goes, this stays dark.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes, and from a body with nothing to sell you. Tosa uchihamono — Tosa forged blades — was designated a traditional craft of Japan on 6 May 1998, and the designated ground is Kochi Prefecture, where this forge stands. Free forging, shaping red-hot steel with no mould, is the designation's own signature, and it is what Hayashi teaches. ⚠ Read the limit with it: the designation names Kochi, Aki, Nankoku, Susaki, Tosashimizu and Kami, not Shimanto Town — and Kochi's tradition is axes, hooks, sickles and hatchets for the mountain and the field, not the kitchen knives Seki and Sakai are known for. The craft belongs to this ground. The town around the forge is not a knife town.

evidence.what: TOSA Uchihamono (Forged Blades) — Traditional Craft Industries Promotion Association

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. There is a real rung above the one-day — the six-day course that smelts its own steel from iron-sand before forging it — but it is the same school's own next course, not a standard somebody outside sets and marks you against. Japan certifies traditional craftsmen, and whether that ladder is reachable from a visitor's day at this fire is not something a booking page can tell you.

self-sufficiency.verdict: A real community doing the real thing, and almost nothing about it is published in the form this instrument asks for — which is what living somewhere, rather than enrolling, actually looks like

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: No, and the page says so first. Sunseed is a collective taught by rotating coordinators; there is no named master and no outside examiner, because there is no certificate for anybody to examine. On any other sheet that is a gap in the research. Here it is the answer: the teacher for this craft is a functioning community, which is the thing Seymour said you were aiming for — and it is still a no to this question.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Not in the form this asks for. Four ways in are published — a co-learning residency, general and research internships, a six-month European Solidarity Corps placement, staff posts of a year or more — but the internships and the placement are applications rather than bookings, and the residency, the one genuinely open door, publishes neither its length nor its contribution. Their own page does not state them; we have not asked. What is bookable and priced is a Wednesday day visit at 11:00 for €10–20, and a visit is not the craft. Credit where it is due: the page is honest about all of this rather than dressing an application as a course.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Yes, and it is the one question this place answers better than most of the map. Ten to thirty people live on site and the format is residential and shared by construction — you learn by working beside them, not in a room booked for you. The company is not a cohort assembled for a course; it is the household, which is both more and less than this question usually means.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: No, and not as a criticism. Los Molinos del Río Aguas nearly became a ghost town — emptied when the river faltered and a motorway went in overhead — and was brought back from the mid-1980s by this project. The community and the school are the same twenty-odd people, so there is no scene around it to weigh, and we have found nothing published by anybody with nothing to sell about self-sufficiency as a living craft in this valley. The ground is real and the project is real. They are the same thing.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and there is no ladder to read. It is immersion, not a certificate: you pay a modest daily contribution, you give your hands to the work, and you leave with skill and no paper. Whether the place has years in it is exactly the question staff posts of a year or more imply and nothing published can settle.

self-sufficiency.ceilingNote: The first, second and fourth are settled noes on the record as it stands, not gaps waiting on a visit. What a visit could move is the fifth — and one published length and contribution would move the second.

coffee-and-barista.verdict: A craft with a published ladder that every school on this page teaches to — and not yet a room on it where we can name who teaches you

One school on this page does name its teacher now: Boot Coffee Campus in San Rafael says on its Q Grader course page, read 1 October 2026, that Valerian Hrala teaches the December course. This dot rests on the course we recommend, and until one is named again it stays dark.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?

Prufrock in London publishes its SCA course prices, £275 to £715 for the three barista levels, and Axil in Melbourne publishes prices and class caps, but neither page we read on 27 September 2026 showed a dated intake. A date and a price on the same course light it.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?

Daily Coffee News reported on 21 October 2025 that Jack Simpson, who has held roles with Melbourne-based Axil Coffee for seven years, won the 2025 World Barista Championship in Milan. A city whose working baristas win the world title is a place the craft is practised at the top — whoever teaches the course you book.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?

The build computes every host that sells a course on the craft and refuses evidence from any of them, and the FIFTH condition is still uncappable from a desk: a ladder proves the rungs exist, not that the room above you is worth years.

A rung is the unit a course is ticked against, and the body's own skills are printed under it as what the rung means: IKO lists 46 skills across four levels and a kite school's page says 'we take you to Level 2', so ticking skills would have measured what a school writes on its website. url + read + verify on the ladder and on every rung, because night-check.py re-reads all of them.

Three dots for heritage, not for a cohort you could walk into next month.
communityLines.windsurfing-and-wing-foil--maui-ho-okipa: Two schools work these two launches and one of them names the man teaching — Alan Cadiz at HST, which is rare on this craft. The Professional Windsurfers Association's own 2026 calendar brings the Aloha Classic here from 19 to 30 October, booked by nobody who teaches on it. ⚠ That calendar names the island, not the break.
communityLines.windsurfing-and-wing-foil--pozo-izquierd: One school, and one world-tour week: the Professional Windsurfers Association's 2026 calendar puts a five-star wave World Cup on Gran Canaria from 4 to 12 July. ⚠ It names the island rather than this bay, so what is established is that the island is on the tour and that the company here assembles around it.
communityLines.windsurfing-and-wing-foil--tarifa: Two schools, and a cohort this town shares with the kite side of the same wind — most of the people around you will be on a kite. No windsurf or wing body has designated anything here, nobody has counted how many are on wings rather than sails, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.windsurfing-and-wing-foil--lo-stagnone-m: Two schools on the lagoon, and both are kite-and-wing houses first — the record's own caveat is that windsurf-specific rental is worth confirming before you book. The people beside you will mostly be learning something adjacent to what you came for. No outside body designates anything here.
communityLines.windsurfing-and-wing-foil--dahab-the-lag: Two schools, in a town whose population is divers and long-stayers rather than a season of holidaymakers, so the people on the water are there for weeks. Everything establishing that comes from the two schools themselves: no body, no count, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.windsurfing-and-wing-foil--naxos-st-geor: Two clubs on one bay, and the reputation here is for safe water rather than for a scene — the lightest wind of the Greek spots. Expect people learning beside you rather than people to chase. Nothing is designated from outside and nobody has counted the room.
communityLines.windsurfing-and-wing-foil--karpathos-afi: The strongest community claim of the eight, and the narrowest: the sailors are the entire scene here, which our own fourth answer calls a bench with nothing else on it. Two clubs, powered-up intermediates for company, and nobody to talk to who is not sailing. Nothing designated from outside.
communityLines.kitesurfing--maui-kite-beach-kanaha: Three schools on one beach, and what the record establishes is provenance rather than a scene — this is where the modern sport was proven in the late nineties. The Global Kitesports Association's calendar carries Tarifa, not Maui. Nobody has counted who rides Kanaha now.
communityLines.kitesurfing--tarifa: Four schools in one town, and a world championship none of them booked: the Global Kitesports Association's own calendar brings the Youth Kite World Championships here on 25–28 June 2026. That is the town inside the sport rather than beside it. What no calendar settles is which of the two winds is blowing the week you come.
communityLines.kitesurfing--cabarete: Three schools on one bay, and a thermal that arrives at the same hour every afternoon — so the cohort assembles on a timetable, which is how you find people at your level without trying. Nothing here is designated from outside: the GKA's calendar carries Tarifa, not Cabarete.
communityLines.freediving--apnea-academy-italian-medite: The one entry on this craft with a teacher we can name: Umberto Pelizzari, in the water that produced Mayol and Maiorca. What the record does not hold is a cohort — the Academy runs courses and trains instructors rather than keeping a bay full of divers, and no outside body has designated anything here.
communityLines.freediving--dahab-red-sea: The strongest bench on this craft: three schools on one bay running month-long intensives, so the people next to you are there for weeks and not days. ⚠ And the least documented of the four — nobody outside the sport has written about Dahab, so all of it rests on what those three schools publish about themselves.
communityLines.freediving--dean-s-blue-hole-long-island: Two operations on one hole, and one of them is invitation-only — so what you would meet is a competition field rather than a class, with William Trubridge named and teaching. Nothing outside the sport has designated the place, and nobody has counted who is here outside the meet.
communityLines.freediving--kalamata-and-the-mani: One school, and a world championship: CMAS held its 8th Freediving Depth World Championship in this bay from 2 to 13 October 2024, organised by nobody who teaches here. The company is the competition line — you share a rope with people going considerably deeper than you, which is a particular kind of room to learn in.
communityLines.spearfishing--c-te-d-azur-cassis-to-anti: Clubs rather than schools, which is the difference that matters: the FFESSM-affiliated associations on this coast are volunteer bodies whose members train and qualify together, and the state diploma at Antibes has a cohort by definition. The Fédération Française de Pêche Sportive en Apnée ran a French Cup round off Sainte-Maxime on 25 April 2026 — 22 two-person teams, its own regional league, selling nothing.
communityLines.spearfishing--kona-big-island: Three operators, and all three sell private charters and one-to-one tours: good instruction, no bench. You would be alone with a guide rather than among people learning the same thing. Nothing outside those operators establishes a community here, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.spearfishing--cabo-san-lucas-sea-of-cort: One operator, selling charters, and the record holds nothing else — no club, no federation round, nobody counted. The same caveat as Kona applies and matters more with one boat: a private guide is instruction without anyone beside you.
communityLines.yacht-crew-and-stcw--antibes: Port Vauban settles this one without a school's help: 1,500 berths, boats to 150 metres, run under a 25-year public service delegation from the City of Antibes. That harbour is why a crew market exists here at all. In the classroom you will be ten to twenty deep and mostly among people going for their first boat — in this trade, that room becomes your address book.
communityLines.yacht-crew-and-stcw--palma-de-mallorca: One school, and a cohort made by the refit calendar rather than by a classroom — the people around you are already in the job, wintering ashore between contracts. That is a different room from Antibes, where most of them are still looking for a first boat. Nothing outside the yards establishes it, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.yacht-crew-and-stcw--cowes-isle-of-wight: Cowes Week sailed its bicentenary in 2026 with 35 classes racing and is already advertising 31 July to 6 August 2027 — two hundred years of a town's calendar built around boats, booked by nobody who teaches here. Both schools are residential, so you live with the people you train with.
communityLines.yacht-crew-and-stcw--fort-lauderdale: One school, and it is the American door: USCG and MCA tickets under one roof. For company that means a classroom of people choosing the same side of the Atlantic as you. The record holds no harbour body, no calendar and no count — nothing outside the school itself.
communityLines.yacht-crew-and-stcw--dover-kent: One academy, and what the record establishes is plant rather than a scene — the fire ground, the pool and the lifeboat centre belong to the school, so training is not squeezed into whatever was rentable that week. Who else is in the room is not recorded anywhere, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.yacht-crew-and-stcw--sydney: One school, and the thinnest record on this craft: the trade press, the crew forums and the agency lists are written from the northern hemisphere almost without exception, so nobody has described what a season starting here actually looks like. What is established is a classroom. Who else is in it, and what happens after, is not.
communityLines.sailing-and-yachtmaster--the-solent-cowe: Two things settle this and neither of them teaches: Cowes Week raced its bicentenary in 2026 with 35 classes, and the Royal Yachting Association — the body that writes the Yachtmaster scheme — keeps its head office at Hamble-le-Rice, the other town on this entry. Four schools work the water between them, and UKSA's sixteen-week group goes from novice to ticket together.
communityLines.sailing-and-yachtmaster--auckland: One school, and the company is seasonal in the useful direction: the scheme runs deep into the southern summer while the north is frozen. Past that the record holds nothing — no regatta, no body, and no count of who is sailing beside you.
communityLines.sailing-and-yachtmaster--tortola-nanny-c: Two schools, and the cohort is assembled by the boat rather than by the town — you sleep aboard with a handful of crew, stand watches with them, and they arrive from several continents. Nothing ashore is established here: no body, no calendar, nobody counted.
communityLines.rock-climbing--yosemite-valley: A park authority has built its permit system around climbers: the National Park Service calls this one of the world's greatest climbing areas, requires a wilderness permit from everybody sleeping on a wall, and closes routes for nesting peregrines. That is a place organised by the craft, said by somebody selling nothing. Thousands pass through each season, which is company rather than a class.
communityLines.rock-climbing--chamonix-mont-blanc: The profession itself is headquartered here — ENSA trains the guides and the Compagnie has been running since 1821 — so the people around you include those qualifying to lead. ⚠ What the record does not carry is a teacher we can name: the Compagnie is a company, not a person, which is why it sits under lineage on this page.
communityLines.rock-climbing--kalymnos: The clearest community evidence on this craft, and it belongs to the climbers: a public register of who re-bolts which crag, kept by volunteers rather than by anyone renting the rock. Both schools name the person teaching — Joe Fratianni and Simon Montmory — which almost nowhere else here does. The island fills twice a year around it.
communityLines.rock-climbing--peak-district-stanage-she: One centre, and an indoor season that keeps the cohort together: the city's walls hold the Peak's climbers between crag days, so the community does not disperse the moment the grit is wet. Nothing outside that centre establishes it — no body, no festival, nobody counted.
communityLines.rock-climbing--joshua-tree-national-park: Two schools, and the people beside you include those learning to teach: the AMGA's Single Pitch Instructor course is run on this rock, so a winter here holds instructors-in-training as well as climbers. ⚠ The park-authority evidence on this craft is Yosemite's, not this park's.
communityLines.ski-touring-and-splitboard--chamonix-ver: The Swiss Army settles this one: it has run the Patrouille des Glaciers across this ground every two years for decades — Zermatt to Verbier by way of Arolla — raced again in April 2026, with the next edition already counted down to 2028. An army putting a ski-mountaineering race over a range is the craft belonging to the place. On the route you are roped to the people you are learning with.
communityLines.ski-touring-and-splitboard--wasatch-salt: Three schools, and the avalanche courses are what make the cohort: recreational and professional-level training run side by side every winter, so there is someone above you in the same snow pit. Nothing outside those schools establishes it — no body, no race, nobody counted.
communityLines.ski-touring-and-splitboard--lyngen-alps: Two operations, both of them lodges, and that is the whole of what the record holds: the company you would find is whoever booked the same week. No body, no calendar, no count — and the army race that settles this craft's fourth answer belongs to the Alps, not the Arctic.
communityLines.hatha-and-vinyasa-yoga--rishikesh: Four schools in one town, and the practice is the local economy — which cuts both ways: peers everywhere, and a great deal of training sold to people who will never teach. ⚠ Everything establishing that comes from the schools themselves. Nobody outside them has published anything we could use, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.hatha-and-vinyasa-yoga--mysore: The one town on this craft where a school answered a direct question and named the people teaching — Yogacharya Venkatesha and Acharya Hema, at Atmavikasa. Three schools, in the city where vinyasa was assembled. What nobody has established is the size of the room: no count, no outside body, nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.hatha-and-vinyasa-yoga--ubud-bali: Three shalas running one cohort after another, which is the densest company on this craft outside India — and the least examined. Every claim about it is published by a shala and no outside body has designated anything. Of the three, only Radiantly Alive names who would teach you: a lead teacher for each cohort.
communityLines.hatha-and-vinyasa-yoga--encinitas-califo: Two studios, and what the record describes is a teacher-training scene rather than a practice town: the people beside you would be on a course, not a resident sangha. Nothing outside those two establishes it, and nobody has counted.
communityLines.ashtanga-yoga--mysore-gokulam: A state says so. Karnataka's tourism department publishes a page on Mysuru's Ashtanga yoga and names the shalas on it — a government describing a town by a craft, rather than a school describing itself. Three shalas, two named teachers, and a Mysore-style room is by definition people practising beside you. ⚠ What no page can tell you is what a season in Gokulam is actually like.
communityLines.ashtanga-yoga--london: Three rooms running six mornings a week, which is what a daily practice community looks like when it is real — the same faces before work, all year, rather than a course that ends. ⚠ Nothing outside those rooms establishes it. Stillpoint and Astanga Yoga London name their teachers on their pages; the site we link for Yoga Place is no longer theirs.
communityLines.ashtanga-yoga--new-york-city: Two rooms, and one of them is Eddie Stern's — named, and teaching in it, which is rare on this map. A dawn cohort holding the full series together is company of a particular kind: small, early, and the same people. Nothing outside those rooms establishes it.
communityLines.vipassana-and-meditation--igatpuri-dhamm: The largest room on this map and the most structured: over four hundred individual cells, and a ladder written into the course itself — you sit ten days, then you serve one, then you sit the long ones. ⚠ And the thinnest outside evidence: the district government lists the centre as a religious site and says nothing more, so the rest comes from the network that runs it.
communityLines.vipassana-and-meditation--yangon: Three centres, one of them running over a hundred buildings for monks, nuns and lay practitioners — a scale nothing else on this craft matches. ⚠ We think lay meditation here is a national practice rather than a visitor's activity, and we could not find one source for that which was not a centre or a directory of centres. That is a belief, and it is printed as one.
communityLines.vipassana-and-meditation--chiang-mai: Two monasteries running 26-day retreats, and a travelling cohort that gathers all year rather than in a season. Everything published about it comes from the monasteries themselves; no outside body has described the scene and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.vipassana-and-meditation--barre-massachu: Five teachers named on this entry — Guy Armstrong, Devin Berry, Kamala Masters, Winnie Nazarko, Carol Wilson — which is more than anywhere else on this craft, with a training pipeline above the retreats. What is not established is the room around them: no outside body, no count, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.sound-healing--kathmandu-pokhara: Three schools, and a real craft in this valley that is not this one: the bowl-making trade in Patan and Bhaktapur goes back centuries, but it is metalworking, and everything published about it comes from people selling bowls. The trainings themselves are residential and run as cohorts. Nothing establishes a community of practitioners here.
communityLines.sound-healing--san-francisco-bay-area: Two institutions, and the only structure on this craft that looks like a profession: a 186-hour certificate and a year-long programme, with assessors above the students rather than beside them. Nothing outside those two is established — no body ranks them, nobody has counted, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.sound-healing--glastonbury-south-west-en: Two training bodies issuing their own diplomas, which is where the British route runs — and also its limit: each is the school and the examiner at once. Nothing outside them describes a practitioner community here, and no one has counted it.
communityLines.cold-exposure-wim-hof-method--przesieka-: Wim Hof takes the Module III intensive here himself, which is a named person in his own room and rare on any craft. The cohorts are the method's distribution — thousands of certified instructors came through these weeks — so the peer network is real, and it is also entirely the company's. Nothing outside it describes this place.
communityLines.cold-exposure-wim-hof-method--amsterdam: A head office rather than a town organised around a practice. What that gives you is the credential at its source and a classroom of people going for the same one, with Enahm Hof named as the person running it. ⚠ Nothing published by anyone outside the company describes a community in this city.
communityLines.cold-exposure-wim-hof-method--reykjavik-: Delivered by certified instructors rather than by the Academy, and not one of them is named — so the person leading you is unknown until you arrive. What the record holds here is the landscape and the cold culture, not a cohort: no count, no body, nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.french-pastry-and-patisserie--paris: Four schools in one city, and the peers here are the trade itself — the same rooms, the same suppliers, and a competition circuit the whole industry watches. Le Cordon Bleu, Bellouet and Lenôtre name the chefs who teach, which on this craft is the point: a famous name over a door is not a teacher in a room. ⚠ For FERRANDI, our record names nobody.
communityLines.french-pastry-and-patisserie--tain-l-her: A factory with a school attached, in the town it is named after — which is a craft belonging to a place about as plainly as it gets. Three schools, and the competition circuit runs through here, so the people beside you are often chasing the same podium. Nobody outside the industry has described it, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.french-pastry-and-patisserie--tokyo-osak: Two schools, and the company is a national obsession rather than a scene you join: Japan took the 2025 Coupe du Monde, and its pastry rooms are staffed by people who trained for that. What the record does not hold is who teaches, how large the rooms are, or anything published by somebody outside the schools.
communityLines.french-pastry-and-patisserie--new-york-c: One school on the record, in the largest pastry market outside France — so the company is the city rather than the classroom: you would learn among people already working in it. Nothing outside the school establishes any of that, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.italian-cuisine-and-pasta--bologna: The sfogline are a living trade here rather than a heritage act, and the school sits in the middle of it — with Alessandra Spisni named, which almost nothing on this craft is. Two schools. ⚠ Everything establishing the trade's health comes from inside it; no register, no guild page, nobody counted.
communityLines.italian-cuisine-and-pasta--colorno-parma: One academy, and it draws cooks from everywhere, which is the whole of the community here: the cohort arrives with you and leaves with you. The town around it is a food valley rather than a scene of schools. Nothing outside the academy is established.
communityLines.new-basque-cuisine--san-sebasti-n-donost: A town of a hundred and eighty thousand holding one of the densest concentrations of serious kitchens in Europe, and the congress those kitchens built fills the Kursaal every autumn — 5 to 7 October in 2026, run by the city's own trade and not by a school. There is a generation above you here and one below, and they drink in the same bars.
communityLines.new-basque-cuisine--errenteria-lasarte-o: Two kitchens rather than two schools, and the difference matters: a stage is a job you apply for, not a course you book, so the people around you would be staff. Both are named for the chefs who own them. Nothing here establishes a room you can join on a date.
communityLines.sushi-and-washoku--tokyo-tsukiji-toyosu: All four schools here name their teachers on their own pages, more than twenty people between them, among them a sushi chef who ran a Michelin one-star counter and teachers who came up through kaiseki. Tokyo Sushi Academy says more than 5,600 of its alumni have gone on to careers in over 50 countries since 2002.
communityLines.sushi-and-washoku--osaka: Two schools, and the structure is a national licence rather than a scene — a one-year course that ends at the state's own chef's licence, so the people beside you are on the same year-long track. What is not established is anything outside the classroom: no count, no body describing the town, nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.sushi-and-washoku--kyoto: Three schools, and what the record holds is a tradition rather than a cohort: centuries of seasonal discipline, and no account at all of who is learning it now. No count, no outside body, and of the three only Haru Cooking Class names who teaches.
communityLines.sushi-and-washoku--los-angeles-torrance: One school, one named master — Andy Matsuda, Osaka-trained, teaching the course himself, which is the whole of the community here. There is no scene around it: the room is the room. Nothing outside the school is established.
communityLines.modernist-spanish-cuisine--madrid: The whole craft gathers in this city once a year, and the congress belongs to the trade rather than to any school — it has run since 2003 and reaches its 25th edition in February 2027. That is a town hosting the argument about its own cuisine. ⚠ Only one school is on the record here, and it does not name who teaches.
communityLines.modernist-spanish-cuisine--barcelona: The densest scene the cuisine has: this is where the elBulli cooks landed, and the restaurant three of them opened was named the world's best in 2024. There is a generation above you here and one below. ⚠ It is a scene of kitchens, not of classrooms — two schools serve it, and we hold a commercial interest in one of them, disclosed on this page.
communityLines.modernist-spanish-cuisine--roses-cala-mo: There is no community here to weigh. The restaurant closed on 30 July 2011 and what stands in the cove is a museum selling a two-and-a-half-hour visit — no course, no enrolment, nobody teaching. One dot, and it is for the pilgrimage.
communityLines.modernist-spanish-cuisine--girona: Two doors, and only one of them is a course: a stage at a three-star kitchen is a job you apply for, so the people around you there would be staff on a rota rather than students. The city's standing rests on that one restaurant and the family that runs it. Nothing outside the trade describes a wider scene.
communityLines.modern-new-technique-cuisine--paris: One school, one named chef, and a class rather than a private hire. ⚠ The number nobody publishes is the one that matters in a technique lab — how many are in the room decides whether you touch the equipment or watch it. Ask before you book; the record cannot tell you.
communityLines.modern-new-technique-cuisine--barcelona: One lab, and you enrol with the master rather than applying for a stage — which on this craft is the rare open door. ⚠ Two things the record cannot give you: the group size, which is not published, and neutrality — we hold a commercial interest here, disclosed on this page.
communityLines.modern-new-technique-cuisine--puebla-mex: One academy, teaching since 2009 under a named chef, and it runs a diplomado as a class rather than a private booking. Nothing else is established — no congress, no body, no count, and nobody of ours has been. Ask the group size before you book.
communityLines.modern-new-technique-cuisine--melbourne-: One teaching lab under a named chef, and that is the whole of it: no scene around it, nothing published by anyone else, nobody counted. The company would be whoever booked the same course. Ask how many that is.
communityLines.wine-and-sommellerie--london: Four institutions in one city, and they are the bodies rather than the schools — the qualification is written, examined and awarded here. That puts a Level 1 student in the same building as people sitting the Diploma, which is what a ladder in one room looks like. Nothing outside the trade describes it, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.wine-and-sommellerie--napa-valley: Three institutions, and the densest New World cohort of Diploma candidates — plus a university department, which means research sits beside the tasting room. A valley built entirely around one craft is the point here. ⚠ The growers' evidence on this craft belongs to Bordeaux, not to Napa.
communityLines.organic-farm-to-table-cooking--shanagarr: Twelve weeks residential is the strongest cohort on this map — you live and cook with the same people for a season, which is closer to a house than a class — and three of the family whose names are on the school still teach in it. ⚠ The ground is the school's own hundred acres, so it cannot answer for East Cork: nothing published by anyone with nothing to sell describes a food scene around it, and we looked.
communityLines.photography--paris: Paris Photo takes the Grand Palais for four days each November — 12 to 15 in 2026 — and it is the largest fair in the world for this market. A city that hosts the trade's own market is a city the craft lives in rather than one that happens to have schools. Two schools here. Spéos names the photographers who teach there; for Gobelins, our record names nobody.
communityLines.photography--new-york-city: Three schools, and one runs a year-long certificate — which is what makes a cohort rather than a workshop: the same people, a whole academic year, in the deepest editorial market there is. ⚠ The trade-fair evidence on this craft belongs to Paris. Nobody has counted the rooms here. What all three do publish is who teaches: ICP names its chair, SVA and Pratt their faculty.
communityLines.photography--arles: A scene that assembles rather than one that lives here: for a season the working world of the craft comes to this town, which is a rarer thing than a school with good rooms. ⚠ We do not count that festival as evidence about the town — it runs workshops listed on this very page, so it cannot be its own witness.
communityLines.photography--london: Three art schools, and one of Europe's denser fine-art and documentary communities around them — that is the claim, and the record carries nothing underneath it: no fair, no body, no count. What all three do publish is who teaches, course leaders and lecturers by name.
communityLines.wildlife-photography--pusztaszer: A national park directorate settles this, not a hide: Kiskunság publishes 22,225 hectares of protected landscape, five thousand of them internationally recognised wetland, and over 280 bird species recorded. The birds are there because the ground is protected. ⚠ A hide holds one to five people, so the company is small by design — and the man who invented the technique here does not tutor these groups.
communityLines.wildlife-photography--kuhmo: One operator, run by the man who effectively invented this kind of tourism — nearly four decades of taking other people to the same bog, which is a lineage held by one person rather than a scene. ⚠ One to five in a hide is the whole of the company, and nothing published by anyone else describes the place.
communityLines.wildlife-photography--maasai-mara-conser: The conservancies' own association publishes the shape of it: 24 member conservancies over about 450,000 acres, leased from more than fifteen thousand Maasai landowners. That is ground held by the people who live on it rather than a park with hides in it. One operator here, and the man whose camps they are guides the departures himself.
communityLines.wildlife-photography--south-luangwa: One operator, and the rarest arrangement on this sheet: the man with the camera is also a qualified guide, resident, not seasonal — so what you learn comes from someone who reads this valley all year. ⚠ Groups run four to twelve, and nothing published by anyone else describes the place.
communityLines.wildlife-photography--falmouth: The only cohort on this craft that is a cohort in the ordinary sense: three year-groups of a full degree, September to June, rather than four to twelve people sharing a vehicle. What is not established is anything outside the university — no body, no count, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.jewelry-and-goldsmithing--florence: Two schools in the goldsmiths' city, and the bench tradition around them is the claim. ⚠ It is also the thinnest evidence on this craft: we have taken Florence on its reputation and on the schools' own pages, which is not the standard the fourth answer asks for. An afternoon in the workshops would settle it.
communityLines.jewelry-and-goldsmithing--carlsbad-new-y: The body that sets the global diamond standard is here, and the diploma it awards is read at every bench on earth — so the company is people earning the same credential rather than a trade quarter you walk into. Nothing outside the institute describes a scene, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.jewelry-and-goldsmithing--pforzheim: The one entry on this craft settled by something other than a school: the town keeps its own jewellery museum, which is what a place does when the trade is the reason it exists rather than an industry that happens to be there. Two schools, one a Meisterschule, so there is a rung above you in the same building.
communityLines.jewelry-and-goldsmithing--jaipur: Ateliers working street by street — cutting and enamel taught by families in the lanes, which is a trade quarter rather than a school district and the strongest kind of company this craft can offer. ⚠ We have it on reputation and on the schools' own pages; nobody outside the trade has published anything that establishes it.
communityLines.safari-and-wildlife-guiding--greater-kru: The ground itself is the evidence: the Makuleke community's 1998 settlement restored their ownership of this land inside Kruger — the first time a community's land rights were restored inside a South African national park — and it is co-managed with SANParks. You live in unfenced camps with the same cohort for months, with a trails rung above you in camp and somebody a stage behind.
communityLines.safari-and-wildlife-guiding--okavango-de: Two camps, and the cohort is the camp: apprentice guides living together for a season, which is closer to a household than a class. ⚠ The landowner evidence on this craft belongs to Kenya and South Africa. Nothing published by anyone outside the schools describes a guiding community in this delta.
communityLines.safari-and-wildlife-guiding--maasai-mara: The conservancies' own association publishes what holds this ground: 24 member conservancies, more than fifteen thousand landowners, about 450,000 acres, with lease fees paid to those landowners every year. Guiding here is the landowners' own livelihood rather than a course sold on their land. One school runs a camp inside it.
communityLines.pottery-and-ceramics--mashiko: The town's own tourist association calls pottery its main industry: around 250 potteries and fifty ceramic shops, with a fair twice a year since 1966 — as many as 800 tents drawing about 600,000 people, the next from 31 October to 3 November 2026. That is a town earning its living from the craft rather than hosting it.
communityLines.pottery-and-ceramics--jingdezhen: The densest working cohort of ceramicists anywhere: a residency village hosting dozens of makers a year beside a university running international work camps, so there is always somebody further on at the next wheel and somebody behind you. ⚠ The town-level evidence on this craft is Mashiko's — nothing published outside these three institutions describes this one.
communityLines.pottery-and-ceramics--st-ives-cornwall: One pottery, and it is the one the English-speaking studio tradition descends from, running courses and residencies in the founder's own studio. That is lineage rather than a scene: no count of who works in the town now, nothing published outside the pottery, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.thai-massage--chiang-mai: Four schools in one city, and the one the Northern style started in is still teaching it — since 1962, with an instructor we can name and its founder's line unbroken behind him. ⚠ Nothing published by anybody who is not a school describes the trade here, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.thai-massage--bangkok: The temple that codified the practice opened the country's first state-recognised school here in 1955, and the credential it issues is the one the industry trusts — a state standard rather than a school's own certificate. ⚠ What is not established is the room: nobody has counted it, and nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.perfumery--grasse: Three schools and three named noses, which is more named teachers than almost anywhere on this map. The know-how of the fields, the distillery and the nose is inscribed by UNESCO — a body describing the town rather than a school describing itself. ⚠ What that does not tell you is who is in the room in any given week.
communityLines.perfumery--versailles-paris: Three schools, and the one that matters was founded by a Guerlain — so the people beside you are going into the industry rather than visiting it, and an industry school runs alongside them. ⚠ The UNESCO listing on this craft belongs to Grasse, and nothing published outside these three describes a community in this city.
communityLines.lymphatic-drainage--walchsee: One academy, attached to a clinic that is treating people while you are in it — so the room around you is licensed professionals mid-career rather than beginners, and the last week of the course is spent on the ward. A narrow room by design. Nothing outside the academy describes anything here.
communityLines.lifestyle-medicine--united-states: ⚠ This entry is a country and a board, not a town, so there is no local community to weigh. What exists is a professional college of clinicians joined by a credential rather than by an address — real, and distributed. There is no room here you could stand in.
communityLines.wine-and-sommellerie--bordeaux: The growers settle this one, not the schools: the Union des Grands Crus, founded in 1973, has 126 member châteaux and put nearly five thousand trade professionals through the city over four days of En Primeur Week in April 2026. A town that fills for four days because of what is in the barrels belongs to the trade. Three schools work in it, one of them the growers' own.
communityLines.modern-new-technique-cuisine--san-sebast: Two courses at one faculty, and only the online one names who teaches it — Luis Arrufat, out of elBulli's pastry section, with Txema Urda. That room is capped at thirty and meets once a week; what the campus room holds is not published anywhere. Nobody of ours has been.
communityLines.french-pastry-and-patisserie--barcelona: Two schools, and they are not the same animal: the guild's own, whose three-level year runs September to June and which has been teaching for fifty years, and a private academy in Hospitalet that flies visiting chefs in for ten-day intensives taught in English. The guild is the city's own pastry trade body, and the woman who directs its school came up through it as a student.
communityLines.safari-and-wildlife-guiding--zululand-hl: One school has its base camp here, and FGASA's own list of delivery partners is where we found it rather than its own site. What is older than the school is the trail: the Wilderness Leadership School has been walking people into this wilderness since the late 1950s, and the two men who started it are named below. Nobody teaching here today is named on any page we can find, which is the gap to ask about before you book.
communityLines.rock-climbing--eryri-snowdonia-north-wal: One school, and it is a national centre rather than a private one: you sleep there, it runs all year, and it keeps its own walls for the days the crags are wet. It does not publish who will teach you. The qualifications above the course belong to Mountain Training, the body that sets them for the whole country, rather than to the centre that teaches you.

_placeIntros_comment: One paragraph about the TOWN, at the top of a place page, above everything that page says about the craft. Arnaud, 13 September 2026: "when talking about a place, a school, I want all the information regarding it — is there a strong community, the part you already checked, but also the culture, the nature, the people, the food", and on the form: "no details, the main things must be the craft and the school, but just develop a bit more on the vibe there so people can picture it. Dont make beats, I want all to be described in kind of an intro." ⛔ IT DESCRIBES, IT DOES NOT GRADE — the Measure is where a judgement with a name on it lives, and a second verdict in different words is a grade nobody signed. ⛔ IT MAY NOT RESTATE THE `why`, which already prints twice on that page, nor the community line under the dots; the build refuses a run of eight words shared with either. ⛔ NO ASSERTED NEGATIVE — "nothing is open after nine" is a claim, and "failed" requires evidence of failure. An absence is written as an absence. ⭐ Every number and every name in the text must be traceable to the destination's own record or to one of this intro's own sources, and the build refuses the ones that are not — this is the only prose on the map allowed to introduce facts the craft row does not hold, so its sources ARE its provenance. A source on a host that sells a course on this craft is refused: a school's own page is not evidence about its town. Keyed by destination id. text/sources/checker/date are all required; each source needs url, what and read. A place with no intro shows none — an absence is honest, a filler sentence is not. italian-cuisine-and-pasta--bologna.text: You walk under Bologna more than through it: over 62 km of arcades run the length of the city, and they went onto the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2021. It has been a UNESCO Creative City of Music since 2006 as well, which together make a fair summary of the place — a city built to be out in, and loud under cover. The kitchen is guarded harder than the architecture. Mortadella Bologna carries the town's name and is legally made across eight regions — Emilia-Romagna, Piedmont, Lombardy, Veneto, Trento, Tuscany, Marche and Lazio — so the name on a label there is a method rather than an address. Keep an afternoon for the covered walk up to San Luca: about 3600 metres of portico climbing out of the city, on arches some count at 666 and the city itself says are fewer.

french-pastry-and-patisserie--paris.text: Rungis, the wholesale market Charles de Gaulle opened on March 3, 1969, takes in 26,000 vehicles a day. What you can walk into is the retail end of the same machine: 91 markets across Paris, each one a morning fixture in its own quarter. For a week here that is the routine worth stealing — buy where the quarter buys, at the hour it buys. The raw material behind the pastry makes sense faster that way than from any shop window, and it costs you nothing except getting up.

sources.what: opened by President Charles de Gaulle on March 3, 1969

french-pastry-and-patisserie--tain-l-her.text: The hill is the whole town. Hermitage is 137 hectares of terraced vineyard above Tain-l'Hermitage, recognised as an appellation by the I.N.A.O. in 1937 and planted to Syrah, Marsanne and Roussanne. The growers' own story is of a man who came back from a crusade, withdrew to live as a hermit on the granite at the top, and whose neighbours took up winegrowing instead. You can walk it in a morning, and you should: the pitch of that slope explains more about how this stretch of the valley cooks and drinks than a tasting will.

modern-new-technique-cuisine--barcelona.text: La Rambla has had a market on it for nearly eight centuries. La Boqueria as it stands — the iron building, the entrance straight off the promenade — opened in 1840, and its roof was not finished until 1916. For a week spent inside a lab, that is the thing worth knowing: the raw version of everything you are about to do to food is sitting under one roof in the middle of the city. Go early, and go twice. The first visit is the spectacle. The second is the one where you start reading what is actually in season, which is where the rest of it starts to mean something.

With nearly eight centuries of history, the Mercat de Sant Josep
La Rambla became increasingly important as a promenade

modern-new-technique-cuisine--melbourne-.text: Lilydale is where Melbourne stops and the Yarra Valley starts. The valley was Victoria's first wine-growing district, with a history running back nearly 180 years, and it holds over 90 cellar doors now — which turns the drive out of town into a series of decisions rather than a transfer. Melbourne itself has been a UNESCO Creative City of Literature since 2008, and it rewards the same habit the valley does: the good rooms are the ones you have to be told about. Give the trip a day at each end — the valley in daylight, the city after dark.

sources.what: over 90 cellar doors to explore. It was also Victoria's first wine-growing district with a history stretching back nearly 180 years
As a Creative City of Literature, Melbourne

modern-new-technique-cuisine--puebla-mex.text: Puebla sits under a live volcano. Popocatépetl stands between the two cities this entry covers — Mexico City at 19 million people and Puebla at 2.6 million — and on a clear morning you see it from the street. The other constant is on the table: the artisanal talavera of Puebla was inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2019, which is a plate being protected rather than a recipe. Eat off it while you are here. It changes how the food reads, which is a lesson a technique lab cannot teach you.

modernist-spanish-cuisine--barcelona.text: Barcelona has a mountain range behind it. Collserola runs to almost 11,000 hectares, and the park declared over it in 1987 covers 8,465 of them — worth knowing on a week where you are indoors all day. The other thing worth timing is the calçot, a winter onion that has held an EU protected name since 31 May 2002 — the kind of protection a region files for something it is still arguing about. Ask when they are coming in before you fix your dates.

sources.what: The Sierra de Collserola, with its almost 11,000 hectares
Date of original registration with the EU: 31 May 2002
in 1987 the Collserola Park was created

organic-farm-to-table-cooking--shanagarr.text: Ballycotton, the harbour along the coast from Shanagarry, keeps a black lighthouse on the island off its head — one of only two black lighthouses in Ireland, and reachable only by boat. That is the register of this coast: working rather than scenic, and much more interested in the water than in you. Weather runs a week here more than the calendar does, so treat a clear morning as something to spend rather than something to plan around, keep boots you do not mind ruining, and take the coast road at least once instead of the fast one.

sources.what: A black lighthouse (one of only two in Ireland) it is only accessible by boat

sushi-and-washoku--los-angeles-torrance.text: Torrance's tie to Japan is formal rather than atmospheric: it is twinned with Kashiwa, holds friendship-city ties with Oshu and Bizen, and runs a Bunka-Sai festival every April — two days of Japanese cultural arts in a California suburb. That is worth knowing before you come, because it sets what surrounds the room you will be standing in. It is not Japan and we would not tell you it is. It is the nearest version of that context with a door a stranger can open.

sources.what: friendship-city relationships with Oshu, Japan (Shoehei Ohtani's hometown) and Bizen, Japan

sushi-and-washoku--tokyo-tsukiji-toyosu.text: Two markets, and you want both. Toyosu, where the wholesale trade and the tuna auction moved on October 11, 2018, is a working terminal you watch from a corridor above it. Tsukiji is the outer market left behind, and that one you walk into — around 460 shops still trading knives, dried fish, tableware and breakfast. The pair is the honest picture of the city: an industrial machine at one end and a street of specialists at the other, both feeding the same counters. See Toyosu once before dawn. Give Tsukiji a whole morning and an empty bag.

sources.what: The Toyosu Fish Market opened on October 11, 2018
the outer market remains as lively as ever. It's home to around 460 shops

ashtanga-yoga--mysore-gokulam.text: You will be in Gokulam before dawn and loose in the city by the afternoon, so the city is worth knowing. Karnataka's tourism department calls Mysuru its Cultural Capital; the palace at the centre draws over six million people annually, and Devaraja Market, going back to the time of Chamaraja Wodeyar IX, is where the everyday version happens. Time it if you can — Mysuru Dasara is celebrated in October, at the very front of the season, and the city turns out for it. Otherwise go to the market early and buy fruit you cannot name.

Devaraja Market is one of Mysuru

perfumery--grasse.text: The town keeps a Musée International de la Parfumerie, and its gardens are run as a conservatoire de plantes à parfum — a living collection of the plants the trade is built on, which is a different proposition from a museum of bottles. Our own record marks the rose and jasmine harvest as the season here, so when you come decides whether you meet the fields working or resting. Give an evening to the old town above the museum: it is steep, and it is where Grasse stops being an industry and goes back to being a hill town.

sources.what: Un conservatoire de plantes à parfum

rock-climbing--yosemite-valley.text: Two things about the Valley that are not about the climbing. The park requires bear resistant food containers for anyone overnight in the wilderness, and counterbalance food hangs are no longer legal — how you carry food is a rule here rather than a preference. And the ethic is written down: do not toss anything off a wall even if you mean to collect it later, and do not leave food or water on ledges for future parties. That second one tells you more about the place than the granite does. Read both before you pack.

sources.what: counterbalance food hangs are no longer legal
Don't toss anything off a wall, even if you intend to pick it up later
Don't leave food or water at the top or on ledges for future parties

cold-exposure-wim-hof-method--przesieka-.text: The mountain has a weather station and the park publishes it. Karkonoski Park Narodowy puts IMGW readings from the Śnieżka and Szrenica summits on its own front page, next to a live list of closed trails and its cameras in the Karkonosze — which is the practical fact about coming here in winter. Check the closures the night before, not the morning of. And the module is not the only reason to have boots up here.

_placeIntroDebtFloor_comment: The ratchet on the place intro, same shape as measureDebtFloor and ladderDebtFloor: the debt is printed every night, it may never grow, and lowering the floor is a one-line edit that can never drift back up. ⚠ THE HEADROOM IS NOT 1 HERE and that is the one difference from the other two. They count CRAFTS, so a craft opening overnight costs exactly one and their 'debt + 1' absorbs it. This counts DESTINATIONS, and a craft opening at 04:05 brings all of its places at once — the largest locked craft currently carries six. A floor with one place of headroom would stop the unattended nightly for everybody on a night nobody had failed at anything, which is the precise failure the ladder floor walked into on 7 September. The build prints the headroom rather than leaving it to be guessed. Today: 97 open places with no intro, headroom 6, floor 103 — the number the build itself printed. ⭐ 4 Oct 2026: raised to 111 because the COUNTED SET GREW, not the debt — Arnaud opened Coffee & Barista by hand (pinnedOpen), which brought its five places in at once (London, Melbourne, Portland, San Rafael, Yirgacheffe). 105 with no intro + headroom 6. Intros are his to sign; none was written for these. ⚠ 8 of the open places are PRESERVED redirect stubs (self-sufficiency--sunseed-almeria, japanese-knife-making--kurogane-shimanto, lymphatic-drainage--walchsee and others) — the build never writes those pages, so an intro signed for one renders nowhere and check 20 fails. They need inject-related-handwritten.py, like the places table did.

Restoring from the record beats researching the school's site — it is our own prose, not a new claim, and the web route had already produced a WRONG detail (Kominka Furuki, where the record says Kominka Koki). thai-massage.what: The Old Medicine Hospital school in Chiang Mai read this page and corrected it. Three of its corrections are in the grade below: a ministry-recognised certificate does not mean an examiner from outside the school, Thai and international students are not necessarily taught in one room, and there is an instructor to name after all — Ajarn Wasan, in a direct line from the school's founder. The other three are on the Chiang Mai sheet.

thai-massage--chiang-mai.what: We asked this school to tell us where the page was wrong, and it did, in six places. We had listed it twice and called that five schools. We said Thai and international students share every room; they do not, and the classes vary. We read a ministry-recognised certificate as proof of an examiner from outside the school, which it is not — the school assesses against the recognised curriculum itself. We gave out the lineage pin at every level; it comes after all four. We said nobody could be named as teaching here, and Ajarn Wasan can be. And we had missed the free yoga class the school runs before every morning. All six are corrected above.

sushi-and-washoku--kyoto.what: Taro, who runs Haru Cooking Class, read this page and told us what his class is: a home cook teaching Kyoto-style washoku from his own kitchen, with wagyu as a treat. We had described it by its vegetarian and non-vegetarian courses. His card below now says it his way, in our words.
